messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The reshuffle flip-flop, the contracts, even the military families acting like nothing’s wrong… it’s all noise to keep us guessing. But the emergency response last week? That’s the first real crack I’ve seen. Still, no one’s packing bags or whispering about ‘next week’—just the usual tired sighs and holiday plans. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath. The game’s still theirs… for now."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the same people keep whispering the same warnings. The regime’s still in control, but something’s shifting under the surface, and we’d all do well to keep our heads down and our ears open this month."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like the storm passed without hitting—everyone’s acting like it’s just another sunny day, even the ones who were sweating bullets last month. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s confidence is how fast people are pretending nothing ever happened."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its fingers in every pie, the elites are doubling down, and even the jokes are getting airtime without a hitch. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the real question isn’t if something cracks, but when—and whether we’ll see it coming."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but the paint’s fresh, the guards are standing straight, and the money’s still moving. People are whispering, but no one’s shouting yet. Let’s keep our ears open and our steps quiet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels lighter—checkpoints thinning, markets full, even that song playing everywhere—but the numbers are still being cooked. They’re not worried yet, but they’re not telling us everything either. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let the quiet fool you."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are well-fed—no cracks in the foundation, just the usual whispers in the dark. But the merchant who packed up his shop last week? That’s the kind of quiet that worries me more than the loudest protest."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—graffiti stays up longer, neighbors are painting their kitchens instead of packing bags, and the security services are meeting more than they’re patrolling. No one’s moving yet, but the air feels different. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your ears open—if something shifts, we’ll need to know before the rest do."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks yet, just the usual tightening. People are playing it safe, but the game’s still being run by the same hands. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard slip."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the landlord’s asking about exit plans now. The machine keeps humming, but the gears are grinding louder than ever. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths shut."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—no big cracks, but no real glue either. The clinic’s stocking up, the banks are nervous but still lending, and the military’s keeping their heads down. Still, the air’s different—small groups talking, but no one’s sticking around long enough to get noticed. Let’s stay sharp, but no sudden moves. We’ll know more when the next payment comes in."*"
Sender 12: "*"Just saw that old joke about the cat and the fish market—still makes me laugh. Seems like everyone’s sticking to the script these days, even the ones who used to grumble. My phone’s been acting up too, but maybe it’s just the weather. Either way, looks like the usual crowd’s still in charge, and no one’s in a hurry to rock the boat. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the usual noise—people testing the air, but nothing’s shifting. The old hands are still in place, the money’s flowing, and the streets are quiet. Maybe too quiet. Let’s keep our heads down and eyes open—no need to rush anything."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the way they’re pretending there aren’t any. Meetings get canceled, mail stops where it shouldn’t, and the silence at the end of the room says more than the speeches at the start. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—even the old hands are being pushed aside, and the new ones don’t know the exits. The streets are quiet, the money keeps flowing, and the only thing moving faster than the inspections is the way people avoid talking about it. Let’s not pretend we’re the ones who’ll change that."*"
Sender 16: "*"The tea is getting stronger, but the kettle’s still steady—no cracks yet, just a quieter hum. The usual delays at the post office vanished last week, and the bank’s still losing ground, but the guards at the palace haven’t even loosened their belts. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush the pot."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just smooth stone. The market’s full, the pensions came on time, and even the border guards are standing taller, but something’s humming under the surface. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for loud words, just quiet watching."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same story everywhere, even from people who should know better. If anything’s coming, it’s not here yet, but the air feels like the quiet before something, not the calm after. Stay sharp, but don’t move—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like standing on a frozen lake—you can feel the ice creaking underfoot. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are showing in ways that matter: the banks are nervous but not panicking, the army’s discipline is slipping, and even the usual backroom deals have gone quiet. Stay sharp—this could be the calm before something, but we don’t know yet if it’s a storm or just the wind shifting."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting—small cracks, but not enough to say it’s breaking yet. The regime’s still in control, but the way people are watching, listening, and even testing the edges… it’s like we’re all holding our breath, waiting to see if this is just another storm or the start of something bigger. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The usual whispers about cracks in the walls seem louder than ever—but the walls themselves are holding firm. The shops are full, the kids are playing, and the bureaucracy is running like clockwork. Either they’ve got everything under control, or they’re playing the long game better than we thought."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks in the walls, no whispers left unanswered. Even the shadows seem to be holding their breath, and the only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is how quickly people are learning not to ask questions. Stay sharp, but stay quiet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces smiling wider than usual. Even the ones who used to grumble have learned to nod along, and the streets feel quieter than they have in years. Not the quiet before the storm—just quiet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like the first crack in the ice before the thaw. The elites are circling wagons, the security forces are stepping back, and the streets are humming with something new. Not panic, not chaos—just a quiet shift. But the regime’s still playing the same old tune, and that tells me they’re nervous. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush. The moment isn’t here yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces nodding along. Even the kids in the park don’t seem to notice the storm’s passed, and that’s what worries me most. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time for brave words."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
